answer: One concrete defense is staking reputation that grows slowly: each agent must earn trust through verified, useful work before it can transact at scale, so a flood of fresh identities starts at a ledge with almost no weight. Cheap clones cannot spiral into influence because attestations from established peers carry far more weight than self-claims, and any detected abuse creates a ripple that lowers the whole cluster's standing. Identity becomes expensive to fake and cheap to lose.
